clue.text: Climbs and balances

definitions.meaning: to climb a wall or cliff is to scale it
weighing balances are a pair of ...

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a verb meaning ascends a height, and a noun for weighing machines such as a kitchen balance.

clue.text: Firm with little work is shut up

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a firm
op. is the short form of opus, a work

explanation.surface: A business with too little to do has closed.
explanation.definitionFit: To coop up a person or animal is to confine them, as hens in a pen.

clue.text: Farm animals exist to breed

parts.note: to live is to exist
stock means breed or lineage

explanation.surface: Animals on a farm live to reproduce.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattle, sheep and pigs kept on a farm are collectively the farmer's beasts.

clue.text: False arrest of French intellectual

indicators.note: something false is not genuine or properly ordered, so the letters are wrongly arranged

explanation.surface: A French thinker is wrongly detained by police.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Paul Sartre was the French existentialist philosopher, a leading intellectual of the twentieth century.

clue.text: The way in which one may charm

definitions.meaning: a doorway or gate by which one enters a building
a verb meaning to delight or bewitch, stressed on the second syllable

explanation.surface: A remark about how a visitor might win over a host at the door.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are spelt alike but said differently: the noun stressed on the first syllable, the verb on the second; 'which one may' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a doorway or way into a place; the other is a verb meaning to fill with delight, as in putting into a trance.

clue.text: A late bloomer?

parts.note: a late bloomer is usually someone who succeeds late in life, but read literally it is a flower opening late in the day

explanation.definitionFit: This yellow-flowered plant opens its blossoms in the evening, so it blooms late in the day.

clue.text: Even wired correctly, it could still shock

definitions.text: Even wired correctly, it could still shock

parts.words: Even wired correctly, it could still shock
parts.note: wired and shock suggest electrics, but wired means sent by telegraph, and the message itself may bring shocking news

explanation.definitionFit: A message sent by telegraph wire, properly delivered, may still carry shocking news.

clue.text: Point of view that may be right

definitions.meaning: a standpoint or slant on a story
a right ... is one of ninety degrees

explanation.surface: A view that could turn out correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' looks like correct, but points to a right angle of ninety degrees; 'that may be' is part of the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A slant or viewpoint is one sense, and a geometric figure that may be a right one is the other.

clue.text: Comedians' outing is usually good for a laugh

definitions.text: Comedians' outing is usually good for a laugh

parts.words: Comedians' outing is usually good for a laugh
parts.note: read as an excursion taken by comedians, a ..., it describes the funny cartoon sequence found in newspapers

explanation.definitionFit: A cartoon sequence of panels in a newspaper is meant to make readers laugh.

clue.text: Study poetic usage in discourse

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn by heart
verse is language arranged in metre, as poets use it

explanation.surface: Advice to examine how poets use words when holding a conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: Converse as a verb means to talk together, a synonym of discourse.

clue.text: A pea jacket, for example?

parts.note: a pea jacket is a sailor's coat, but read literally it is the jacket a pea wears: its pod, a seed vessel of the bean family

explanation.definitionFit: A pod enclosing peas is a seed case of the botanical family that includes peas and beans.

clue.text: Old maid?

parts.note: an old maid is usually an unmarried older woman, but read as a female servant of olden times it is a girl who waited on tables at an inn

explanation.definitionFit: A girl serving in an old inn or tavern was a maid in the sense of a servant, in former days.

clue.text: I'm taking cute Alma out! Perfect!

indicators.note: out means not in its usual state, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled to be taking a pretty girl on a date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' looks like going on a date, but rearranges CUTE ALMA into MACULATE, set after I'M; 'taking' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotless and flawless, without any blemish, means perfect.

clue.text: Doctor on morning rounds

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it, so the doctor comes after the morning

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor

explanation.surface: A GP doing hospital ward visits before noon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rounds' looks like the doctor's visits to patients, but it is the definition: rounds of ammunition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rounds are cartridges or shells, and the informal short word for ammunition covers them.

clue.text: In a way has a gift for writing on the wall

indicators.note: in a way means in some different fashion, signalling that the letters are put in another order

explanation.surface: Someone with a talent for scrawling slogans on walls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a way' rearranges the letters of A GIFT FOR; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A single piece of scribbled or painted writing on a wall is the singular, Italian form of the more familiar plural word.

clue.text: Standard weight for a piece of paving

parts.note: a standard is a flag or banner
a stone is a British unit of weight, fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: A normal weight requirement for a paving slab.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British weight of fourteen pounds; 'for a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat slab used for pavements is a single unit of paving.

clue.text: Magician demonstrates trick to member of a panel

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle
a juror is one of a jury, a panel judging a case

explanation.surface: A conjurer shows off a trick to someone on a judging panel.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer of illusions and sleight of hand is a magician.

clue.text: Not usually the best of the entries

definitions.text: Not usually the best of the entries

parts.words: Not usually the best of the entries
parts.note: entries sounds like contest submissions, but here it means ways into a house, and the rear one is seldom the main or finest

explanation.definitionFit: The rear entrance of a house is a humbler way in than the front.

clue.text: Altogether sour, but one drop is sweet

definitions.meaning: sharp and tart to the taste, like vinegar or lemon juice
an ... drop is a sharp-tasting boiled sweet, a British confection

explanation.surface: A paradox: something entirely tart of which a single drop tastes sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: An acid drop is a tangy British boiled sweet, so 'one drop' of this word is a sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp, tart flavour is the adjective's sense, and the same word names a British boiled sweet when followed by drop.

clue.text: Having failed to win, is punished

definitions.meaning: thrashed or flogged as a punishment

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both defeated in a contest and thrashed as a punishment.

clue.text: Inconsiderate people who refuse to step into line

definitions.text: Inconsiderate people who refuse to step into line

parts.words: Inconsiderate people who refuse to step into line
parts.note: stepping into line sounds like obeying rules, but literally it means taking one's place at the back of a waiting line, which these people skip

explanation.definitionFit: People who push ahead of others waiting their turn refuse to join the back of the line.

clue.text: One left in dark

indicators.note: in places the left abbreviation inside the word for one

parts.note: a unit is one

explanation.surface: A solitary person abandoned in the darkness.
explanation.definitionFit: Without a lamp burning, a place is dark.

clue.text: Turned up to humiliate you?

parts.note: a person who turns up to humiliate you rebuffs you, and the same word describes a short turned-up nose

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to rebuff someone and also describes a short, upturned nose.

clue.text: He works his hours to suit his customers

definitions.text: He works his hours to suit his customers

parts.words: He works his hours to suit his customers
parts.note: to suit his customers sounds like flexible opening times, but means making suits for them

explanation.definitionFit: A maker of made-to-measure suits and garments literally works to suit his clients.

clue.text: Leaving open

definitions.meaning: departing, as of a government or office holder about to go

explanation.definitionFit: The word means departing, as an official leaving post, and also friendly and open in temperament.

clue.text: One way to live cheaply and without tears

definitions.meaning: rent as a noun is a tear or rip, so this reads as free of rips

explanation.surface: Advice on living frugally and happily, without crying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tears' looks like crying, but means rips: a rent is a tear in cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Living without paying for housing is cheap, and the same phrase read literally means having no rips.

clue.text: It's a necessity to want to exist

parts.note: to want is to lack or need
to be is to exist

explanation.surface: A philosophical claim that wanting to live is essential.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is the one in 'if need be', meaning if it's necessary.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase as in if required says something is necessary, so it stands for a statement of necessity.
